ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low; high-intensity pixels (white and off-white) associated with scarring and barnacles constitute approximately 5-8% of the total visible surface area relative to the dominant low-intensity black pigmentation.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous solid black pigmentation across >90% of the surface; discrete high-contrast yellowish-white clusters at the far distal tips (coordinates: top-left and top-right margins); sparse white linear and punctate disruptions scattered throughout the medial and lateral fields.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression with an internal angle of approximately 35-45 degrees; vertical depth occupies ~20% of the fluke's total visible vertical profile.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, high-amplitude serrations characterized by multiple sharp, irregular peaks and valleys along the entire continuous upper boundary of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave trailing edge curve trending upwards and outwards from the median notch toward the distal tips; the lower leading edge visible at the bottom is convex.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Two dense, high-contrast clusters of roughly circular off-white/yellowish pixel groups located at the extreme distal tips of both lobes, representing localized rugosity.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Numerous distinct white linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) oriented horizontally and diagonally, most prominent on the lower-mid sections of both the left and right lobes.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Visible irregular tissue architecture at the distal tips associated with high-contrast clusters; multiple fine-line scars across the ventral surface.
other_distinctive_markers: A prominent, isolated circular white ring mark (ocellus-like) located in the mid-outer region of the left lobe, and a distinct deep indentation/nick on the upper-mid trailing edge of the left lobe.
